conclusion: In this simulation, at a 0.1% fault budget per service, services A, B and C averaged 99.900% of probes passing, an annualized estimate of about 8.8 hours down per year each, while probes through the A to B to C chain passed 99.696% of the time, about 26.6 hours a year, about 3.0x the per-service mean.
setup: in-process simulation, virtual clock, fixed seeds from 9009; 3 services A calls B calls C with 1 to 3 ms simulated hops; each service up or down per a schedule of random non-overlapping outage windows of 100 to 400 ms (all windows, including the last, kept in that range) totalling 1%, 0.1% and 0.01% of each run; simulated probe every 50 ms for 20 simulated minutes (24000 probes per target); single-service values are the mean of A, B and C; annualized downtime = simulated failure ratio x 8760 h, assuming that ratio represents a full year (says nothing about outage timing); no real HTTP servers, process stops or health-check code; compressed-time simulation on one Mac, not a production measurement
